name: JW Marriott Hotel Beijing Central
positioning: JW Marriott hotel in Beijing's Xicheng District, a base for the Forbidden City, Tiananmen Square and the hutongs
best_for: Travelers who want a central base for Beijing's historic sights
Longer stays in a suite with a full kitchen

facts.text: The hotel is at 18 Xuanwumenwai Street in Beijing's Xicheng District.
From the hotel in Xuanwumen, guests can visit the Forbidden City (Palace Museum), Tiananmen Square and the National Museum of China.
Qianmen Street, the Temple of Heaven, Liulichang Cultural Street and the hutongs are nearby to explore.
Xuanwumen and Caishikou metro stations serve Lines 2, 4 and 7.
Rooms have plush bedding, spacious bathrooms and 24-hour in-room dining.
Executive Rooms include a workspace and access to executive lounge services.
The JW Marriott Executive Lounge has a dedicated outdoor space.
The hotel has a heated pool with a lifeguard on duty.
The fitness center is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and its facilities include sauna rooms and steam rooms.
Man Ho is a Cantonese restaurant with private dining rooms.
Casalingo is an Italian restaurant and wine bar serving signature pizzas.

highlights.text: A hotel experience lets guests print with a 300-year-old technique and carve their own name seal.
Sky Garden Suites have a balcony with city views.
The hotel offers Grand Rooms with a hutong view.
Residence Suites have a full kitchen for longer stays.
The Lounge serves themed afternoon tea, coffee and a selection of gin in a space with Chinese-inspired design.

considerations.text: The hotel is about 35 km from Beijing Capital International Airport.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning in a central location.
WhataHotel notes the urban setting may bring typical city noise.
